messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV-cache continuous-batching error rate spike detected on prod-inference-cluster (region: us-west-2). 90%ile latency breaching SLO. Alerts: KVCACHE_MISS_RATE, BATCH_SIZE_P25 drop. Links: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/2087654321
oncall-sre-amy: I'm grabbing it. Seeing big spike in kvcache misses and batch fragmentation. Totals: miss_rate x8, avg_batch_size down from 12 -> 1.8.
carla-dev: hitting it now. Any recent deploys to runtime?
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: inference-runtime@v4.3.7 -> v4.3.8 by @frank-eng at 2087653600.
ben-ml: Noted - we rolled a small change to structured output marshalling (escape/unescape) yesterday. Could be related: changed how function call tokens are emitted, might break prefix matching in KV keys.
frank-eng: I pushed the marshalling patch. It was meant to fix JSON arrays in funcall output. Rolling back if needed.
oncall-sre-amy: Can we confirm if tool/function-calling traffic has a higher error rate? Logs show a surge in single-token batches for requests labeled "funcall-structured".
emily-support: Customer Impact: two customers (acme-inc, travelly) reporting increased 500s and timeouts in chat endpoints. CS is on calls.
dan-platform: Dump from a node (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] kvcache: miss key=funcall:1583... size=0 tokens, fallback=true
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] batching: created batch size=1 route=funcall-structured
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] runtime: latency spike child process 0x4f2
```
carla-dev: This looks like the structured output is adding nondeterministic prefixes so cached keys don't match -> cold KV lookups and tiny batches.
ben-ml: Hypothesis: the new marshalling added a variable whitespace or order in keys used to compute prefix hash. That would fragment cache and cause continuous batching to break.
oncall-sre-amy: Mitigation plan: (1) throttle function-calls / structured routes to reduce stampede, (2) revert marshalling on runtime as a hotfix, (3) switch affected traffic to fallback model variant (v4.3.6-compat) with existing marshalling, (4) if needed, restart K/V cache process.
frank-eng: I'm ready to roll back the change. Which service? inference-runtime or marshaller sidecar? The patch was in the marshaller module inside runtime.
carla-dev: Easiest immediate action: insert a request-level prefilter to normalize structured outputs so kv keys are stable. I can push a config change to the request preprocessor. Small patch, no binary change.
oncall-sre-amy: Doable. Prioritize throttle + prefilter first to stop bleeding. Revert only if traffic still bad.
emily-support: CS: pushing note to impacted customers that we're mitigating and expect improvement in ~10-15m.
frank-eng: Performing config push: prefilter.normalizer=on to preproc-cluster via k8s configmap update. Command: `kubectl apply -n prod -f prefilter-normalizer-208765.yaml`
deploy-bot: Config applied: prefilter-normalizer set=on on preproc-cluster (rollout id: r-8f3a).
carla-dev: Also applying rate-limit rule for funcall routes: `route.funcall-structured.max_qps=50` in gateway.
deploy-bot: Gateway config applied, new policy instantiated.
ben-ml: Metrics coming in: batch_size_p50 recovering from 1.9 -> 7 within 90s, kvcache miss_rate down by 65%. Latency improving: p95 dropping from 1.9s -> 0.8s.
oncall-sre-amy: Good. Any residual 500s? emily_support?
emily-support: Tickets show error rate dropped ~80%, but Acme still seeing sporadic timeouts for a subset of routes. They've been routed to fallback model as of 2087654270.
frank-eng: I'm standing by to revert runtime marshalling if post-mitigation metrics don't hit targets in 10m.
carla-dev: Also adding short-term telemetry: tag requests with marshaller_version header so we can attribute hits. Pushing that now.
deploy-bot: Telemetry patch rolled; new spans include marshaller_version.
ben-ml: Correlation shows 98% of errors came from marshaller_version=v4.3.8; v4.3.6-compat almost unaffected. This confirms root cause.
oncall-sre-amy: Okay decision: keep prefilter + throttle, schedule an immediate rollback of the marshalling change and a canary rollback to 10% for 15m. Frank please execute rollback to v4.3.6-compat on 10% of nodes.
frank-eng: Starting canary rollback: `kubectl set image deployment/inference-runtime inference-runtime=redwood/inference-runtime:v4.3.6-compat --record` targeting nodes subset.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback started. Monitoring policies attached.
ben-ml: After canary, error rates on canary pods = baseline. Full rollback plan ready if canary stays green for 15m.
oncall-sre-amy: Customer update: notifying Acme + Travelly. Thanks @emily-support.
emily-support: Sent updates. Both teams escalated to priority P1 and acknowledged.
carla-dev: Postmortem notes in-progress: add test for deterministic marshaller output, add unit test for prefix stable hashing, and gate marshalling changes behind feature flag.
frank-eng: Canary stable for 12m, p95 stable at 0.6s. Proceeding to scale rollback to 100% in 3m.
deploy-bot: Rollback completed to v4.3.6-compat across prod cluster at 2087654380.
oncall-sre-amy: All clear check: kvcache miss_rate back to baseline, batch_size median ~11. System SLOs restored. Marking incident status: mitigated.
emily-support: Customers notified of resolution. Closing customer-facing alerts.
carla-dev: Follow-ups: postmortem, change control for marshalling, longer retention on kvcache metrics, chaos test that simulates structured-output variability.
frank-eng: I'll open the rollback PR and include the hotfix diff and test.
ben-ml: Will help craft the postmortem hypothesis and test plan.
oncall-sre-amy: Leaving notes: incident_id=INC-2087654321, duration ~27m, primary cause: nondeterministic marshaller changes fragmenting KV cache leading to continuous-batching collapse, mitigation: prefilter normalizer + throttling + rollback.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2087654321 status=mitigated severity=sev2 assignees=[oncall-sre-amy, frank-eng, carla-dev] link=https://incidents.redwood/2087654321 :white_check_mark:
frank-eng: Thanks all. I'll file the PR and ping infra for follow-up action items. :thumbsup:
